title: Guard (GySgt to Pvt) FMOS*, DC PP&O
raw_text:
1.     MOS 8151, Guard (GySgt to Pvt) FMOS*, DC PP&O

    a. Summary. Guards enforce or supervise the enforcement of security
measures and the protection of classified material and United States property
and personnel.

       b.    Prerequisites.   None.

       c.    Requirements

             (1) Not to be assigned to personnel either as a primary or additional
MOS.

             (2) To be used only as a billet designator in T/O's.

       d.    Duties

             (1) Enforces military or Department of State regulations and orders.

        (2) Controls entrances and access to military installations, United
States diplomatic missions, or other designated establishments.

        (3) Verifies authenticity of passes and identification cards of
military personnel, civilian employees, and visitors afoot or in motor
vehicles entering or leaving installations or diplomatic missions.

        (4) Prevents unauthorized removal and theft of United States
Government property.

        (5) Makes periodic checks of standing lights and locked doors and
designated secure areas.

             (6) Receives and verifies guard property.

             (7) Maintains guard property accounts and guard report logbooks.

        (8) Prepares offense, accident, unusual incident, injury reports and
correspondence pertaining to activities of a guard unit.

             (9) Assures that scheduled bugle calls are sounded.

             (10) Conduct guard mount.

             (11) Inspect and instruct guards and sentinels while on post.

        (12) Supervises or assists in the supervising of the guard of the day
during emergency situations.

        (13) Directs traffic, escorts visitors, or vehicles delivering
supplies and equipment.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Security Guards 33-9032.

       f.    Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
